passage: Ujjwal's fists were clenched under the desk. Kishore had grabbed his tiffin again at recess and thrown it in the bin, and the whole back row snorted. That night Ujjwal lay awake seeing Kishore's smirk and imagining, in scary detail, making him feel every second of it. The pictures were so vivid they frightened him. He realised his hatred was as big as the hurt behind it. He didn't want to become someone who does that to another person, or end up in trouble himself. In the morning he told his older sister Radhika everything, his voice cracking. She didn't tell him he was overreacting. "This is not something you should carry alone," she said. "Let's go and see the vice principal together." Ujjwal nodded, and his fists finally opened.

qa.q: What did Kishore do with Ujjwal's tiffin at recess?
qa.a: He grabbed it and threw it in the bin.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal realise about the pictures in his head?
qa.a: He realised his hatred was as big as the hurt behind it, and that it frightened him because he did not want to become someone who does that to another person.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal do that was wise?
qa.a: He told his sister Radhika, shared the anger with her and agreed to go to the vice principal together instead of retaliating.

qa.q: How might Radhika see Ujjwal's anger?
qa.a: As a sign that he has been badly hurt, not as overreacting. She takes it seriously and suggests adult help.

grounding: Ujjwal hates the boy who torments him and pictures hurting him, but shares it with his sister and seeks adult intervention instead of retaliating.

passage:
School counsellor's note, Monday
Zainab came in at lunch, fists clenched. For four weeks Rukmini has been mocking her in class, hiding her bag, and posting a cartoon of her in a class group. Zainab said, "I hate her. I keep imagining pushing her into the drain outside school."
I told her the anger made sense. It is a sign she has been hurt again and again, and that this is not her fault. I asked if she was planning to act on it. She said, "No. I'd get into trouble, and she'd win." I told her that was wise and that hitting back could put her at risk.
I asked what she needed. She said, "For it to stop." With her permission I spoke to the class teacher before the end of lunch. We have saved the cartoon, spoken to Rukmini, and called both sets of parents this afternoon. I will see Zainab again tomorrow morning.

qa.q: How long has Rukmini been mocking Zainab?
What was Zainab feeling when she came to the counsellor?
qa.a: She felt hatred and rage, fists clenched, after weeks of being hurt by Rukmini.

qa.q: What made the counsellor's response wise?
qa.a: The counsellor treated the anger as a sign of harm, checked she wouldn't retaliate, and brought in the teacher and both families that same day.

qa.q: How might Rukmini respond when adults get involved?
qa.a: Rukmini may feel defensive or ashamed, but adult intervention makes it clear the bullying must stop.

grounding: A teen who hates the classmate tormenting her and imagines hurting her shares the anger with a counsellor, who arranges adult intervention.

passage:
Wednesday night
Today Vikas tripped me in the corridor again and the whole line laughed. That's the sixth time this month. He also took my geometry box and threw it behind the lockers.
I hate him. I lay on my bed and pictured shoving him so hard he'd cry in front of everyone. I pictured it so clearly that it scared me.
I wanted to do it tomorrow. But I know what would happen. He's bigger. His friends would join in. And I'd be the one suspended.
So I told Anna when he came home from college. He listened to everything and said, "Tushar, your anger makes sense. He's hurting you. But you don't fight him alone." Then he called Appa and Amma into the room, and Appa phoned my class teacher right away. She said she'd meet us at 8 tomorrow, before class.
I'm still angry. But I'm not carrying it on my own.

qa.q: How many times has Vikas tripped Tushar this month?
What was Tushar feeling while lying on the bed?
qa.a: Tushar felt hatred and anger strong enough to picture hurting Vikas, and was scared by how clear the picture was.

qa.q: Which choice worked better than fighting back, and why?
qa.a: Telling Anna, who brought in Appa and Amma to contact the teacher, because retaliating could have put Tushar at risk.

qa.q: How does Anna see Tushar's anger?
qa.a: Anna sees it as a natural response to being hurt, but wants adults to step in so Tushar doesn't face Vikas alone.

grounding: A teen who hates the classmate tormenting them and pictures hurting him shares it with a safe person and gets adult intervention.
